coverage.checklistItem: Write down the audit goal, scope, environment, owner, and deadline.
coverage.note: The audit goal, project boundaries, ownership, and deadline must come from the project team.

coverage.checklistItem: Identify the site's purpose, users, critical journeys, sensitive data, and major systems.
coverage.note: Business purpose, user needs, critical journeys, data sensitivity, and system relationships require project context.

coverage.checklistItem: Record any missing access or evidence as a limitation, not a pass.
coverage.note: The runner records incomplete public collectors. The reviewer must also record missing repository, account, environment, and operational evidence.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm the README explains how to set up, run, test, build, and deploy the project.
coverage.note: Repository documentation must be read and tested in the actual project context.

coverage.checklistItem: Build the project and run its normal checks when repository health is in scope.
coverage.note: Project commands can change files, download dependencies, or require services, so the agent runs them only when safe and in scope.

coverage.checklistItem: Review dependency support, secret handling, branch protection, and production access.
coverage.note: These controls require source, dependency, hosting, and repository-platform evidence.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm non-production environments are private and do not use production data unexpectedly.
coverage.note: Environment access and data handling cannot be established from one public page.

coverage.checklistItem: Use the [agent-ready repository checklist](agent-ready-repository-checklist.md) when coding agents will work in the repository.
coverage.note: Agent use and repository instructions require project-specific review.

coverage.checklistItem: Compare the documented architecture with what is deployed and note major maintenance risks.
coverage.note: Architecture and maintenance risk require documentation, source, deployment, and owner evidence.

coverage.checklistItem: Review test coverage for important user journeys and failure cases.
coverage.note: The public runner does not inspect project tests or execute application-specific journeys.

coverage.checklistItem: Test important pages and journeys on representative desktop and mobile layouts.
coverage.note: The profile reviews one desktop homepage. Representative pages, mobile layouts, authentication, and important journeys remain manual or project-owned tests.

coverage.checklistItem: Look for broken links, browser errors, failed requests, mixed content, and stale content.
coverage.note: The runner checks browser errors, insecure resources, homepage content, and a bounded same-host link sample. Wider crawling and content approval remain manual.

coverage.checklistItem: Use the accessibility, security, performance, SEO, or privacy checklist when that area needs a deeper review.
coverage.note: The combined profile provides a public baseline. The agent routes material findings and incomplete areas to the specialist skills; privacy requires project and data-handling evidence.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm ownership of hosting, domains, certificates, vendors, and administrator accounts.
coverage.note: Ownership and account records are operational evidence.

coverage.checklistItem: Confirm the site is backed up and a representative restore has been tested.
coverage.note: Backup contents and restore evidence cannot be verified through a public website review.

coverage.checklistItem: Review monitoring, logging, support, incident response, patching, and vulnerability handling.
coverage.note: Operational procedures require access to the relevant systems, runbooks, and owners.

coverage.checklistItem: Review content ownership and publishing workflow when a CMS is in scope.
coverage.note: CMS governance requires platform access and content-owner confirmation.

coverage.checklistItem: Group related problems and separate confirmed failures from missing evidence and optional improvements.
coverage.note: The report groups public machine observations by area. The agent adds source, operational, and manual findings and interprets their significance.

coverage.checklistItem: Prioritize findings by user impact, security risk, effort, and urgency.
coverage.note: Machine statuses help organize evidence, but final priority requires project impact, likelihood, effort, and timing.

coverage.checklistItem: Give every accepted finding an owner and record any untested areas or follow-up reviews.
coverage.note: Finding ownership, risk acceptance, and follow-up are accountable project decisions.
